plan.title: Group drama, and how you handle it

intake.question: In a group project, you're usually...

options.label: The one who keeps it fun
The one quietly doing the hard part
The one who presents it and shines

intake.question: If you had to be famous for one thing?

strong.text:
With a strong chart, you play your position at full volume. If you're the {pos_lower}, everyone knows it within a week of debut. Your challenge is leaving space for the members who grow slower. A group with one fully lit member and four dimmed ones looks worse on stage than five people at eighty percent.

In practice this means you'd be the member producers hand the hard part to, because you won't crack. Accept it, then hand a piece of it back to someone who needs the confidence. A strong position played generously is how groups last past the seven-year contract.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Full volume suits you. Turn it down one notch for the group.

weak.text:
With a weak chart, you grow into your position rather than walking in with it. The first few months you might wonder if you deserve the spot. You do. Members like you often become the fan favorite in year two, once the shyness wears off and people see how much work you did quietly.

In practice this means you'd ask for feedback more than anyone and quietly improve faster than anyone. Track it. Keep a note of every stage you were proud of, because your memory will try to keep only the mistakes.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Year two is your year. The quiet work shows eventually.

wood.heading: Your element on stage: Wood
wood.text: Wood is growth, and Wood members get better in public. Fans who followed you from debut can see the curve: the shaky first live, the confident third comeback, the stage where everything clicked. Wood energy on stage is upright and reaching, arms that extend fully, a posture that says you're still going somewhere. You also improve fastest with a clear goal. Give a Wood member a skill to learn by next month and they'll have it in three weeks. The danger is impatience with members who grow on a different schedule. Not every tree grows at your speed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood grows in public. Fans love watching the curve.

fire.heading: Your element on stage: Fire
fire.text: Fire is visibility, and Fire members are the ones a camera operator follows without being told. Your expressions read from the back of the arena. Your energy rises with the crowd, so a loud audience makes you better and a quiet one makes you work twice as hard. Fire on stage loves the dramatic moment: the turn, the look, the held note with the arm raised. The danger is burning hot for the first half of a concert and running on fumes for the encore. Pace the flame. Fans remember the ending more than the opening.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fire burns hot early. Save some flame for the encore.

earth.heading: Your element on stage: Earth
earth.text: Earth is reliability, and Earth members are the floor everyone else dances on. You're consistent, comeback after comeback, and consistency is underrated in an industry that loves a viral moment. Earth on stage looks grounded: low center of gravity, steady breath, a calm face during chaos. Members relax when they stand next to you. The danger is playing it safe. Once a year, try something on stage that you're not sure you can pull off. Earth that takes one risk looks like a mountain moving, and audiences never forget it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth is the floor everyone dances on. Try one risk a year.

metal.heading: Your element on stage: Metal
metal.text: Metal is precision, and Metal members are the ones who hit the beat exactly on the beat. Your lines are clean, your angles are sharp and your vocals sit right on the note. Choreographers love you because you execute without drama. Metal on stage cuts: crisp stops, decisive turns, a stare that ends the song. The danger is coldness. Precision without warmth reads as distance from the seats, so let something soft through every stage: a laugh, a wink, a hand reaching toward the crowd.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal hits exactly on the beat. Add one warm moment per stage.

water.heading: Your element on stage: Water
water.text: Water is feeling, and Water members make a stage feel like a mood rather than a routine. You adapt to the song: fluid in the ballad, slippery and fast in the dance track, eerie in the dark concept. Fans describe your performances with weather words. Water on stage is hard to copy because it's never exactly the same twice. The danger is drifting. On tired days your energy can go somewhere else entirely, so build one anchor into every song, a mark you always hit, a look you always give.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water is a mood, not a routine. Keep one anchor per song.

base.your-position:
Gap Wood is the tall pine, and in a group the tall pine is the leader. Not because you asked for it. Because on the first day of trainee life, when nobody knew where the bathroom was, you were the one who found out and told everyone. You stand up straight, you speak first in meetings with the company, and you take the blame when a stage goes wrong even if it wasn't your part.

Your leadership style is protective and principled. You'll argue with a manager about the members' sleep schedule. You remember who was sick last week. You'd rather run one more practice than let the group look unprepared. The other members tease you for being a dad at twenty, and then call you first when something goes wrong.

The position suits you because you think in terms of the whole forest. Your quiet risk is forgetting you're also a tree that needs water.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The tall pine. Of course they made you leader.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Dad energy at twenty. The members love it. Mostly.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You checked on the youngest mid-formation. That's the job.

spring.intro:
You're Wood born in spring, a young tree in a forest that is all growing at once. Element match: the {season} season carries your own element, so your stage energy comes with backup dancers built in. You walk into a group already sure of your lane, which reads as confidence on stage and occasionally as not leaving room for anyone else's solo.

For Gap Wood, this season shapes the kind of leader you'd be: how much you push, how much you shelter, and how long you keep standing before you sit down.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Born with backup. Lovely. Now share the center sometimes.

summer.intro:
Wood born in summer is a tree in full leaf under a hot sky, green and generous and a little thirsty. You pour into the season: your birth season pulls your element outward, into expression. That makes you a performer before you're anything else: you want an audience, a reaction, a camera to find. The cost is energy. You give a full stage every time and then need a very long nap.

For Gap Wood, this season shapes the kind of leader you'd be: how much you push, how much you shelter, and how long you keep standing before you sit down.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You were born to perform. Also born to nap afterward.

earth.intro:
Your Wood arrived in the Earth days that close a season: a tree with its roots wrapped around heavy soil. You shape the season: your element works on the season you were born in, the way a choreographer works on a room full of bodies. You were made for the practice room: setting formations, fixing details, turning a messy run into a clean one. You like results you can see in the mirror.

For Gap Wood, this season shapes the kind of leader you'd be: how much you push, how much you shelter, and how long you keep standing before you sit down.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd fix everyone's formation before your own. Classic.

autumn.intro:
Picture Wood born in autumn: a tree in the season of the axe, when the air turns sharp and the leaves come down. The season tests you: the season you were born in presses on your element, like a strict trainer who never says good job. That pressure made you disciplined. You know your parts, you show up early, and you take criticism like a professional, even when it secretly stings for a week.

For Gap Wood, this season shapes the kind of leader you'd be: how much you push, how much you shelter, and how long you keep standing before you sit down.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your season trained you hard. It shows, in a good way.

winter.intro:
Wood born in winter is a bare tree with its roots deep in cold, wet ground, quietly drinking. The season feeds you: your birth season feeds your element, like a trainee with a great vocal coach from day one. People sense that you were looked after early. You learn choreography fast and recover from bad stages fast, because something underneath keeps topping you up.

For Gap Wood, this season shapes the kind of leader you'd be: how much you push, how much you shelter, and how long you keep standing before you sit down.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Something keeps refilling you. That's why your bad stages never last.

base.your-position:
Eul Wood is the climbing flower, the vine that finds a way up any wall, and in a group that's the main dancer. Your body solves problems your words don't. Give you a formation that doesn't work and you'll find the path through it, bending around the other members like ivy around a trellis.

You're adaptable to a degree that looks like magic. A new choreographer, a last-minute change, a stage half the size you rehearsed on, and you adjust in real time. Members watch you to find their marks. You rarely ask to be the center, but the camera keeps finding you anyway because movement is how you talk.

The position fits because your strength is flexibility with intent. You bend, but you're always growing toward the light. Your risk is bending so much for the group that you lose track of your own shape.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The climbing flower. Of course you're the main dancer.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You'd finish every move a beat late, like honey. Show-off.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Members find their marks by watching you.

base.your-position:
Byeong Fire is the sun, and in a group the sun stands in the center. You didn't campaign for it. You just walked into the first group photo shoot and every light in the room seemed to tilt toward you. Center is the face of the group: first in the formation, first in the music video, the member the general public remembers.

Your energy is open and generous. You hype the members before every stage, wave to the fans in the cheap seats, and laugh loudly at your own mistakes on live television. You make the group feel bigger than five people. Companies love you because you're impossible to dislike. Members love you because you share the warmth, mostly.

The position suits you because you shine without trying. Your risk is the sun's classic problem: it doesn't notice when it's too hot for everyone else.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The sun. The cameras found you before you found your mark.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Messing up on live TV and laughing first. Iconic behavior.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Ending fairy? You can't hide joy. Never could.

base.your-position:
Jeong Fire is the candle, small and steady and impossible to look away from, and in a group the candle is the main vocal. You hold the high note at the end of the ballad. You get the bridge, the part where the song breaks open and the stadium goes quiet. Your power isn't volume. It's that you make thousands of people feel like you're singing only to them.

You're emotionally precise. You hear when the harmony is a hair off, you notice when a member is pretending to be fine, and you sing like you've lived every lyric, even the ones you haven't. Producers trust you with the hardest lines. Members rely on you when live audio is shaky.

The position suits you because your gift is intimacy at scale. Your risk is that candles burn themselves to give light, and you'll do exactly that unless someone tells you to stop.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The candle. Of course the bridge is yours.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Eyes closed on the high note. Show-off. Gorgeous show-off.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You make a stadium feel like a conversation.

base.your-position:
Mu Earth is the mountain, and in a group the mountain is the lead vocal: the voice underneath everyone else's. You hold the harmony while the main vocal flies. You cover the parts people miss on live shows. Without you the songs would wobble, and almost nobody outside the group notices until you're absent and something feels off.

You're steady, patient and calm under pressure. When a live broadcast goes wrong, you're the one who keeps singing like nothing happened. Members lean on you, literally, in group photos and emotionally after bad days. You'd be leader in plenty of groups, and in yours you're the second-in-command everyone actually listens to.

The position suits you because you're the ground the group stands on. Your risk is mountain stubbornness: you can become so fixed in how things are done that change feels like an earthquake.

base_panels.text: The mountain. The voice under every harmony.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Nobody notices the lead vocal until they're gone. Then everyone does.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The stage lift broke and you didn't blink.

base.your-position:
Gi Earth is the garden field, the soil where everything grows, and in a group that's the all-rounder. You sing, you dance, you rap if somebody's sick, you host the variety segment and remember everyone's birthday. You're not the single brightest point in any one category. You're the reason every category works.

You're nurturing and practical. You notice which member skipped lunch and slide a sandwich across the table. You learn everyone's parts so you can cover anything. Producers call you the glue. Members call you when their parents visit, because you're the one the parents like best.

The position suits you because a group is a garden, and you know how to tend one. Your risk is being so useful to everyone that you forget to plant anything of your own.

You're direct, brave and fiercely loyal. You defend the members in public and roast them mercilessly in private. You hold yourself to a hard standard and you expect the group to rise with you. Your lyrics would be blunt and funny and secretly sentimental, which is the main rapper's eternal secret.

The position suits you because you cut through noise. Your risk is that swords cut whether or not you meant to swing, and some of your honest feedback lands like a blade.

The season feeds you: your birth season feeds your element, like a trainee with a great vocal coach from day one. People sense that you were looked after early. You learn choreography fast and recover from bad stages fast, because something underneath keeps topping you up.

For Gyeong Metal, the season decides how sharp the blade comes out of the gate: freshly forged and hot, or cold and polished and ready to cut.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Something keeps refilling you. That's why your bad stages never last.

autumn.intro:
Autumn Metal is the cold, clear air of the harvest month, when blades come out and edges get honed. Element match: the {season} season carries your own element, so your stage energy comes with backup dancers built in. You walk into a group already sure of your lane, which reads as confidence on stage and occasionally as not leaving room for anyone else's solo.

For Gyeong Metal, the season decides how sharp the blade comes out of the gate: freshly forged and hot, or cold and polished and ready to cut.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Born with backup. Lovely. Now share the center sometimes.

winter.intro:
Metal born in winter is a bell in frozen air: clear, cool, and ringing a long way. You pour into the season: your birth season pulls your element outward, into expression. That makes you a performer before you're anything else: you want an audience, a reaction, a camera to find. The cost is energy. You give a full stage every time and then need a very long nap.

For Gyeong Metal, the season decides how sharp the blade comes out of the gate: freshly forged and hot, or cold and polished and ready to cut.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You were born to perform. Also born to nap afterward.

base.your-position:
Sin Metal is the jewel, and in a group the jewel is the visual: the member whose face is on the poster, the bus ad, the thumbnail that gets the click. People assume visuals are just pretty. Fans know better. Being the visual means carrying the group's first impression, every airport photo, every bad angle, every unflattering livestream, and still looking like art.

You're refined, sensitive and quietly perfectionist. You notice the details: a stray hair in the mirror, a lyric pronounced slightly wrong, the lighting that makes a member look tired. You care about beauty because you care about getting things right, not because you're vain. Mostly.

The position suits you because you polish everything you touch. Your risk is that jewels are cut by pressure, and you can be hard on yourself in a way nobody sees.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The jewel. The face on the poster, and the work behind it.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Visual isn't 'just pretty.' It's every bad angle survived.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Small, exact moves. Everything chosen.

spring.intro:
Metal born in spring is a blade in a season of soft green things, sharp where everything else is growing. You shape the season: your element works on the season you were born in, the way a choreographer works on a room full of bodies. You were made for the practice room: setting formations, fixing details, turning a messy run into a clean one. You like results you can see in the mirror.

For Sin Metal, the season decides how the jewel catches the light on stage: polished and gleaming, or still in the setting, waiting for the right angle.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd fix everyone's formation before your own. Classic.

summer.intro:
Summer Metal sits in the forge, hot to the touch and being shaped whether it likes it or not. The season tests you: the season you were born in presses on your element, like a strict trainer who never says good job. That pressure made you disciplined. You know your parts, you show up early, and you take criticism like a professional, even when it secretly stings for a week.

For Sin Metal, the season decides how the jewel catches the light on stage: polished and gleaming, or still in the setting, waiting for the right angle.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your season trained you hard. It shows, in a good way.

base.your-position:
Im Water is the ocean, and in a group the ocean is the producer-member: the one who writes the songs, arranges the harmonies and hears the album before it exists. You might not be the face or the loudest voice. You're the depth. Ideas flow out of you at 3 am, voice memos full of melodies hummed into a phone.

You're big-picture, curious and restless. You think about the group's sound, its story, the concept for three comebacks from now. You get bored with repetition fast and you push the group toward new genres before the company is comfortable. Members trust your taste even when they don't understand your plan.

The position suits you because water finds every gap and fills it. Your risk is that oceans don't like being contained, and you can drift away from the practical stuff entirely.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The ocean. You can hum the whole album before it's recorded.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Voice memos at 3 am, a keyboard covered in snacks.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You improvise a new melody live. The members just follow.

base.your-position:
Gye Water is the rain, soft and everywhere, and in a group the rain is the maknae: the youngest energy, whatever your actual age. Maknae isn't just birth order. It's a role. The member who gets away with teasing the leader, who says what everyone's thinking with an innocent face, who makes the hardest week feel lighter just by being chaotic in the van.

You're intuitive, sensitive and secretly very perceptive. Everyone underestimates you, and you use it. You absorb the group's moods like rain soaking into soil, which means you know exactly who's sad before they do. You're spoiled by the members and you deserve it, mostly.

The position suits you because rain looks small and changes everything it touches. Your risk is staying the baby forever, even when you've grown into someone who could lead.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The rain. The maknae, whatever your actual age.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Teasing the leader with an innocent face. Untouchable.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Giggling one second, dead-serious stare the next.
